title: Wan2.2: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models (repository README)
key_findings: Variants: T2V-A14B, I2V-A14B (MoE, 480P/720P), TI2V-5B (dense, 720P at 1280x704 / 704x1280, 24 fps), S2V-14B (speech-to-video), Animate-14B (motion mimic / character replacement)
A14B MoE: high-noise expert lays out structure, low-noise expert adds detail; switch at half the minimum SNR
TI2V-5B needs >=24 GB without offload; Wan2.2-VAE compresses 4x16x16 (time x h x w)
Prompt extension (Qwen LLM / VLM) recommended for richer detail; I2V may run with an empty prompt
Releases: 28 Jul 2025 (T2V/I2V/TI2V), 26 Aug 2025 S2V, 19 Sep 2025 Animate
practical_applications: Explains why tools/wan.py uses 4n+1 frame counts and 24 fps
I2V prompts can stay short and motion-only because the image carries the scene
limitations: Vendor README; quality claims are the authors' own
No official figure for 6 GB cards: our 480x848 GGUF setting is local experience (CAPABILITY_MATRIX)

title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
key_findings: Diffusion-transformer video model family 1.3B and 14B (Wan 2.1)
1.3B model runs in ~8.19 GB VRAM
Covers up to eight downstream tasks incl. image-to-video, instruction-guided video editing, personal video generation
Authors report 14B outperforms open-source and commercial models on their benchmarks
practical_applications: Background for choosing local open models when quota is the constraint
limitations: Technical report, not peer reviewed at access time; benchmark claims self-reported

title: Wan2.2 Video Generation ComfyUI Official Native Workflow Example
key_findings: TI2V 5B 'should fit well on 8GB vram' with ComfyUI native offloading
Resolution and length set in Wan22ImageToVideoLatent; image input via Load Image node
14B First-Last-Frame workflow (WanFirstLastFrameToVideo) with two LoadImage nodes; tip: write prompts that match both frames
practical_applications: First/last-frame chaining exists for Wan 14B in ComfyUI; our 6 GB card runs only the 5B (no FLF node in tools/wan.py)
limitations: No fps/frame defaults stated on the page

title: AI video prompting guide
key_findings: Formula: [Camera Movement] + [Scene] + [Action] + [Details]; lead with shot type
One action and one primary camera move per 5-10 s clip; avoid 'then/next/after that'
Describe what you want, not what to avoid ('smooth, stable camera movement' not 'no camera shake')
Professionals generate 5-10 variations; spell hard words phonetically for audio
Named moves: dolly, tracking, pan, tilt, whip pan, orbit, dolly zoom, crane, drone ascending, static/locked
practical_applications: Template wording in AI_VIDEO_PROMPT_LIBRARY runway entries
Positive phrasing rule matches our FLUX lesson (negatives summon objects)
limitations: Marketing-site guide; applies to Gen-4 and Veo 3.1 per the page; little on consistency

title: Gen-4 Video Prompting Guide / Gen-4 References (Runway Help Center)
key_findings: Page exists (cited in story-clips/_craft/curriculum/10-ai-video.md, read 2026-11-21); returned HTTP 403 to our fetch on 2026-11-27
practical_applications: Re-read in a browser before relying on Gen-4 References details
limitations: Content not read this session

title: Generate videos with Veo 3.1 in the Gemini API
key_findings: Veo 3.1 Preview models shut down 22 Oct 2026; page points to Gemini Omni Flash or GA Veo on the Enterprise platform
Veo 3.1: native audio always on; 16:9 or 9:16; 4/6/8 s; 720p default, 1080p/4k at 8 s only; 24 fps
image = first frame; lastFrame = end frame (interpolation, needs image)
Up to 3 reference images (person, character or product) to preserve appearance; needs 8 s; not on Lite
Extension +7 s up to 20 times (Veo videos only, 720p)
seed improves but does not guarantee determinism
Prompt elements: subject, action, style, camera position/motion, composition, focus/lens, ambiance; dialogue in quotes, SFX and ambience described explicitly
All outputs carry SynthID watermark; videos stored 2 days
Limits: English best; multi-video reasoning unsupported
practical_applications: Reference-image consistency for a character/product across shots
First/last frame for product rotations between two real photos
limitations: Doc tables conflict for Veo 3 duration/resolution; model availability changed during 2026

title: Veo on Vertex AI video generation prompt guide
key_findings: Elements: subject, action, scene/context, camera angles, camera movements (static, pan, tilt, dolly, truck, pedestal, zoom, crane, aerial, handheld, whip pan, arc), lens/optical effects, visual style, temporal elements, audio, cinematic/edit terms
Negative prompts: avoid 'no'/'don't'; list the unwanted elements instead
For jump cuts keep background, lighting and framing consistent; describe actions in order
practical_applications: Camera vocabulary that Veo documents; matches CAMERA_MOVEMENT ids
limitations: Does not cover reference images or timestamp prompting

title: Luma API — Video Generation (Ray 2)
key_findings: Models ray-2, ray-flash-2
keyframes frame0 (start) / frame1 (end): each an image URL or a previous generation id; enables extend, reverse extend, interpolate between generations
loop true/false; resolutions 540p/720p/1080p/4k; example duration 5s
Camera motion via prompt phrases from /camera_motion/list (e.g. 'camera orbit left'); 'concepts' e.g. dolly_zoom
practical_applications: Chain shots by passing the previous generation as frame0 (continuity)
limitations: Page points to newer Luma API Platform / Agents API; some JSON examples invalid (trailing commas)

title: Sora 2 Prompting Guide (OpenAI Cookbook, archived)
key_findings: Archived recipe (last updated Mar 2026); curriculum 10 records OpenAI docs saying Sora 2 / Videos API shut down 24 Sep 2026
Params: sora-2 / sora-2-pro; size 720x1280, 1280x720 (+1080x1920 etc. on pro); seconds 4-20; input_reference image anchors the first frame and must match size
One camera move + one subject action per shot; concrete verbs ('pedals three times, brakes, stops'); style first
One controlled change per iteration; keep subject phrasing identical across shots; name 3-5 palette colours
Two 4 s clips stitched beat one 8 s clip; shorter clips follow instructions better
Unspecified details are invented; small phrasing changes can alter identity
Template: prose scene / Cinematography (shot, mood) / Actions (beats) / Dialogue
practical_applications: The shot-list prompt template is model-agnostic; reused in AI_VIDEO_PROMPT_LIBRARY
limitations: Service retired; keep as craft knowledge only

title: Kling API — Image to Video (Kling 2.6)
key_findings: Inputs: first_frame (required), last_frame (optional, needs first_frame), prompt text <= 2,500 chars, voice (max 2)
Settings: duration 5 or 10 s; resolution 720p/1080p; audio native/off
First+last frame requires 1080p; native audio cannot combine with last_frame
Images jpg/png, <= 50 MB, >= 300 px, aspect 1:2.5 to 2.5:1; no separate negative_prompt field in 2.6
practical_applications: Product turn between two real kit photos = first+last frame at 1080p, audio off
limitations: Older Kling versions (via third-party mirrors) exposed camera_control, motion masks and image_tail as mutually exclusive; schema differs per version

title: How to animate image parts (Motion Brush)
key_findings: Up to six elements with their own trajectories
Static Brush fixes pixels; add one along the bottom to prevent camera movement
Prompt in 'element + motion' form; one connected region of one category per brush
Impossible trajectories (a building moving sideways) are read as camera paths
practical_applications: Static-brush the glasses, animate hair/fabric only
limitations: No model version named

title: MiniMax Video Generation API — Image to Video (Hailuo)
key_findings: 15 bracket camera commands: [Truck left/right] [Pan left/right] [Push in] [Pull out] [Pedestal up/down] [Tilt up/down] [Zoom in/out] [Shake] [Tracking shot] [Static shot]
Commands in one bracket run together, max 3 recommended; separate brackets run in sequence; explicit commands more accurate than prose
Hailuo 2.3 / 02: 6 or 10 s at 768P, 6 s only at 1080P; prompt <= 2000 chars; prompt_optimizer default true (set false for precise control)
first_frame_image <= 20 MB, short edge > 300 px, aspect 2:5-5:2; separate FL2V endpoint for first+last frame (no 512P)
practical_applications: Only model here with a documented discrete camera-command syntax
limitations: Command list applies only to the named models

title: Seedance 1.0: Exploring the Boundaries of Video Generation Models
key_findings: Native multi-shot generation with consistent subject across shots; joint T2V and I2V
Claims precise instruction following in multi-subject scenes
5 s 1080p in 41.4 s on an NVIDIA L20 after distillation (~10x speed-up)
practical_applications: Multi-shot-in-one-generation is a different consistency route from first/last-frame chaining
limitations: Self-reported; no prompt guide read

title: VBench: Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
authors: Ziqi Huang, Yinan He, Jiashuo Yu, ... Yu Qiao, Ziwei Liu
key_findings: Decomposes video generation quality into 16 hierarchical, disentangled dimensions with tailored prompts and evaluation methods
Provides human preference annotations to validate alignment per dimension
Argues existing metrics do not fully match human perception
practical_applications: Use its dimensions as the vocabulary of our human checklist (subject consistency, flicker, motion smoothness, dynamic degree...)
limitations: Benchmark for comparing models on prompt suites, not a pass/fail tool for one commercial clip

title: VBench repository (VBench, VBench++, VBench-2.0)
key_findings: 16 dimensions: subject_consistency, background_consistency, temporal_flickering, motion_smoothness, dynamic_degree, aesthetic_quality, imaging_quality, object_class, multiple_objects, human_action, color, spatial_relationship, scene, temporal_style, appearance_style, overall_consistency
Custom videos supported for subject/background consistency, motion smoothness, dynamic degree, aesthetic and imaging quality
temporal_flickering requires filtering static videos first
VBench++ adds I2V, Long and Trustworthiness suites; uses CLIP, RAFT, AMT, ViCLIP, LAION aesthetic predictor among others
practical_applications: The 6 custom-video dimensions could be run on our clips if PyTorch/GPU time allowed (not installed)
limitations: Per-dimension model mapping not stated on README

title: VBench-2.0: Advancing Video Generation Benchmark Suite for Intrinsic Faithfulness
authors: Dian Zheng, Ziqi Huang, et al.
key_findings: Five dimensions: Human Fidelity, Controllability, Creativity, Physics, Commonsense (18 fine-grained)
Uses VLM/LLM judges plus specialist anomaly detectors, aligned with human annotation
practical_applications: Adds physics/commonsense/anatomy to the checklist beyond 'looks sharp'
limitations: Preprint; numbers not read

title: EvalCrafter: Benchmarking and Evaluating Large Video Generation Models
authors: Yaofang Liu, Xiaodong Cun, Xuebo Liu, Xintao Wang, Yong Zhang, Haoxin Chen, Yang Liu, Tieyong Zeng, Raymond Chan, Ying Shan
key_findings: Four aspects: visual quality, content quality, motion quality, text-video alignment
700 prompts from real user data, 17 objective metrics
Coefficients fitted to user preference correlate better than a plain average
practical_applications: Weighting automated sub-scores against human ratings — same idea as calibrating our critic
limitations: Weights fitted to their raters and models

title: Towards Accurate Generative Models of Video: A New Metric & Challenges
authors: Thomas Unterthiner, Sjoerd van Steenkiste, Karol Kurach, Raphael Marinier, Marcin Michalski, Sylvain Gelly
key_findings: Proposes Fréchet Video Distance to assess visual quality, temporal coherence and diversity of generated video
Large human study: FVD correlates well with qualitative human judgement
practical_applications: Model-level (set vs set) metric; not meaningful for scoring one clip
limitations: Abstract only; distribution metric needs many samples

title: VideoScore: Building Automatic Metrics to Simulate Fine-grained Human Feedback for Video Generation
authors: Xuan He, Dongfu Jiang, Ge Zhang, ... Wenhu Chen
key_findings: 'None of the existing metric is able to provide reliable scores over generated videos'
VideoFeedback: human multi-aspect scores for 37.6K videos from 11 models
Trained MLLM evaluator reaches Spearman 77.1 with humans on its test set, ~50 points above prior metrics
practical_applications: Evidence that generic metrics/LLM judges need calibration against human ratings for AI video
limitations: Correlation on its own distribution; not tested on Thai social content

title: VMAF — Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion (repository)
key_findings: Perceptual video quality metric by Netflix; libvmaf also computes PSNR, PSNR-HVS, SSIM, MS-SSIM, CIEDE2000
Available as an FFmpeg filter when built with --enable-libvmaf
NEG (no enhancement gain) mode for codec evaluation since 2020; v1 models and HDR models 2026
practical_applications: Compare an export against its master (encode check); not for judging AI content quality
limitations: Full-reference by design (needs the source); README does not list limitations

title: Image quality assessment: from error visibility to structural similarity
authors: Zhou Wang, Alan C. Bovik, Hamid R. Sheikh, Eero P. Simoncelli
key_findings: Introduces SSIM: quality as preservation of structural information rather than error visibility
Evaluated against subjective ratings of JPEG/JPEG2000 images (IEEE TIP 13(4):600-612)
practical_applications: ffmpeg ssim/psnr filters to check re-encodes against the master
limitations: Only the abstract/search summary read; full-reference image metric

title: FFmpeg Filters Documentation (blackdetect, freezedetect, ebur128, silencedetect, psnr, ssim, libvmaf) + ffmpeg -h filter=<name> of FFmpeg 9.0 build
key_findings: blackdetect: d (min duration, default 2 s), pic_th 0.98, pix_th 0.10
freezedetect: n noise tolerance default 0.001, d default 2 s; logs lavfi.freezedetect.freeze_start/duration/end
ebur128: peak=true enables true-peak; target default -23 LUFS; framelog quiet; summary prints I, LRA, True peak
silencedetect: n default 0.001 (amplitude) or dB, d default 2 s
practical_applications: Basis of tools/video_qc.py
limitations: Web page too long to read fully by fetch; option defaults taken from the local binary's help output (FFmpeg 9.0 gyan.dev build)

title: EBU R 128 — Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals (v5.0)
key_findings: Programme loudness target -23 LUFS; descriptors Loudness Range and Maximum True Peak Level
v5.0 Nov 2023 adds supplement s4 for cinematic content; companion Tech 3341 (metering) and 3342 (LRA)
practical_applications: Broadcast reference; social delivery uses the same meter with a louder house target (-14)
limitations: Landing page read, not the full PDF (the -1 dBTP max is from curriculum 12 notes)

title: Recommendation ITU-R BS.1770-5: Algorithms to measure audio programme loudness and true-peak audio level
key_findings: BS.1770-5 (11/2023) in force; specifies programme loudness and true-peak measurement
practical_applications: The algorithm behind ffmpeg ebur128 and loudnorm
limitations: Landing page only

title: Recommendation ITU-T P.910: Subjective video quality assessment methods for multimedia applications
key_findings: P.910 (07/26) in force (prepublished) — the standard for subjective video rating sessions
practical_applications: If the studio ever runs a viewer panel, follow P.910 methods rather than ad-hoc polls
limitations: Only title page read; method details (ACR etc.) not verified here

title: YouTube recommended upload encoding settings
key_findings: MP4, moov atom at front (fast start), no edit lists
Audio AAC-LC/Opus, 48 kHz, stereo
H.264 High profile, progressive, 2 B-frames, closed GOP of half the frame rate, VBR, 4:2:0
Frame rate = recorded rate (24/25/30/48/50/60); 1080p SDR 8 Mbps (24-30 fps) / 12 Mbps (48-60 fps); BT.709
16:9 standard; player adapts to other ratios
practical_applications: youtube_16x9 preset in video_qc.py; ffmpeg -movflags +faststart
limitations: Upload recommendations, not acceptance limits

title: Reels resolution and size (Instagram Help Center)
key_findings: Per search snippet: aspect 1.91:1 to 9:16; minimum 30 FPS; minimum 720 pixels; progressive, H.264 High, 4:2:0
practical_applications: reels_9x16 preset flags < 30 fps as minor (studio clips at 24 fps have uploaded) and < 720 px as critical
limitations: Help page body did not load for our fetcher; snippet only. Third-party guides say feed crops Reels to 4:5

title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
authors: Hu Ye, Jun Zhang, Sibo Liu, Xiao Han, Wei Yang
key_findings: Decoupled cross-attention lets a frozen diffusion model take an image prompt alongside text
~22M parameters; comparable to or better than fully fine-tuned image-prompt models
Transfers to custom models from the same base and to controllable-generation tools
practical_applications: Mechanism behind 'reference image' features: identity/style from an image without training
limitations: Image-level; identity in video still drifts over time

title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation
authors: Nataniel Ruiz, Yuanzhen Li, Varun Jampani, Yael Pritch, Michael Rubinstein, Kfir Aberman
key_findings: Fine-tunes a model on a few images so a unique identifier stands for one subject
Class-specific prior preservation loss keeps general class knowledge
practical_applications: The 'train a LoRA/token for a recurring character' route; heavier than reference images
limitations: Requires training; not set up locally

title: StoryDiffusion: Consistent Self-Attention for Long-Range Image and Video Generation
authors: Yupeng Zhou, Daquan Zhou, Ming-Ming Cheng, Jiashi Feng, Qibin Hou
key_findings: Consistent Self-Attention: training-free consistency across a batch of generated images
Semantic Motion Predictor turns image sequences into smoother, more stable video than latent-only interpolation
practical_applications: Supports 'generate all keyframes of a sequence together, then animate between them'
limitations: Research code; not in our toolchain

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
authors: Lianmin Zheng, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ying Sheng, et al.
key_findings: Biases: position, verbosity, self-enhancement; limited reasoning
Strong judges reach >80% agreement with human preferences, about human-human agreement
practical_applications: Swap order in pairwise comparisons; don't reward longer critiques
limitations: Text chat answers, not video

title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
authors: Peiyi Wang, Lei Li, Liang Chen, Zefan Cai, Dawei Zhu, Binghuai Lin, Yunbo Cao, Qi Liu, Tianyu Liu, Zhifang Sui
key_findings: Ranking flips with answer order; Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT on 66/80 queries with ChatGPT as judge depending on order
Fixes: evidence before score, balanced-position averaging, human-in-the-loop for hard items
practical_applications: Critic writes findings before scores; A/B judged in both orders (creative-critic rule 10)
limitations: Text domain

title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
authors: Arjun Panickssery, Samuel R. Bowman, Shi Feng
key_findings: Self-preference: models rate their own outputs higher than humans would
Self-recognition ability correlates linearly with self-preference; evidence suggests causal link
practical_applications: The maker model must not grade its own prompts/clips; critic gets the work cold
limitations: Text summaries; transfer to vision judges assumed, not shown

title: A Survey on LLM-as-a-Judge
authors: Jiawei Gu, Xuhui Jiang, Zhichao Shi, et al.
key_findings: Survey of strategies to improve and to evaluate the reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge; later versions propose a meta-evaluation benchmark
practical_applications: Index for further reading on judge reliability
limitations: Only search result snippets read

title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability (announcement, NewsNet 1060)
key_findings: 29 Jan 2025: prompts alone do not make AI output copyrightable
Protection can cover human-authored work perceptible in the output and creative human arrangement or modification of AI output
Using AI as a tool, or including AI material in a larger human work, does not bar protection
practical_applications: Studio identity should live in human-authored layers: script, edit, layout, typography, characters drawn/curated by us
limitations: US law; full report PDF did not parse; not legal advice for Thailand

title: 17 U.S. Code § 102(b) — Subject matter of copyright: in general
key_findings: Copyright never extends to any idea, procedure, process, system, method of operation, concept, principle, or discovery, regardless of the form in which it is described
practical_applications: Style/technique (e.g. 'Dutch angle', 'teal-orange grade') is free to use; a specific frame/character/expression is not
limitations: US statute

title: Copyright Act B.E. 2537 (1994), as amended (No. 5, 2022) — DIP English translation and commentary
authors: Department of Intellectual Property, Thailand; Tilleke & Gibbins commentary
key_findings: Per law-firm summaries: protected work = expression of an idea, in a recognised category, original, not illegal (Section 6); ideas, procedures, processes, systems, methods, concepts, principles not protected
Protection without registration; latest amendment 2022 (No. 5) for WCT alignment / online infringement
DIP translations are unofficial; Thai text governs
practical_applications: Same idea/expression line as US for our purposes; get licences for music, fonts, photos
limitations: Statute text not read this session — search summaries of the DIP/WIPO texts and Tilleke commentary only; not legal advice

title: Diffusion Art or Digital Forgery? Investigating Data Replication in Diffusion Models
authors: Gowthami Somepalli, Vasu Singla, Micah Goldblum, Jonas Geiping, Tom Goldstein
key_findings: Image-retrieval framework finds cases where Stable Diffusion blatantly copies training data
Replication rate varies with training-set size and other factors
practical_applications: Prompting 'in the style of <living artist / film>' raises replication and ethics risk; reverse-image-search key outputs
limitations: Abstract only; rates not read

title: Extracting Training Data from Diffusion Models
authors: Nicholas Carlini, Jamie Hayes, Milad Nasr, Matthew Jagielski, Vikash Sehwag, Florian Tramèr, Borja Balle, Daphne Ippolito, Eric Wallace
key_findings: Diffusion models memorise and regenerate individual training images; over a thousand extracted, from personal photos to trademarked logos
Diffusion models less private than GANs
practical_applications: A generated logo/face can be someone's real logo/face: check before publishing
limitations: Abstract only; extraction needed many generations of duplicated training images
